evidence.description: Static shared property with a didSet that triggers a background save without synchronization.

candidates.explanation: The `shared` property of the `User` struct is a static variable that is modified and accessed without any synchronization mechanisms (like locks or serial queues). Since `save()` is called on a background queue, concurrent access to the `User` properties can lead to race conditions.
candidates.title: Thread Safety Issue with Shared Singleton

evidence.description: The save method uses a global utility queue to write the current state to disk.

candidates.explanation: The `save()` method captures `self` and encodes it on a background queue. If multiple property updates occur in rapid succession, the order of completion for the `write` operations is not guaranteed, which can result in an older state overwriting a newer state in the persistent storage.
candidates.title: Potential Data Loss in Asynchronous Save

evidence.description: Force unwrapping the result of a date calculation.

candidates.explanation: The code uses the force unwrap operator (`!`) on the result of `Calendar.current.date(byAdding:...)`, which can cause a runtime crash if the date calculation fails.
candidates.title: Force Unwrapping of Optional Value

evidence.description: Computed property performing decoding on every access.

candidates.explanation: The `stored` computed property performs a full `JSONDecoder().decode` operation every time it is accessed. This is inefficient, especially since it is called during the `init()` process to populate the object.
candidates.title: Inefficient Repeated Decoding
